clue.text: That girl's managed to swallow nothing in food grinder

indicators.note: to swallow means to take something inside, so one piece goes within the other
managed in the sense of handled or worked over, so the letters of the first words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these words, the S included, are the fodder
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl has somehow managed to gulp down nothing at all in a food mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges THAT GIRLS to GASTRLITH, and 'to swallow' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastrolith is a stone swallowed by birds or reptiles that sits in the gut and helps to crush food.

clue.text: Large area runs round European court

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so runs gives hares

explanation.surface: A big expanse where someone sprints around a European court building.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land measure equal to ten thousand square metres, so a large area.

clue.text: Endlessly rebuke male put away for striking boy

indicators.note: put away means removed, so the letter for male is taken out
endlessly means without its final letter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to rebuke is to admonish, to scold

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a man who was jailed for hitting a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts ADMONISH to ADMONIS; 'put away' takes out the M to leave the answer. 'striking' means good-looking, not hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth, so his name stands for any very handsome young man.

clue.text: Old entrance to Salvation Army houses

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the abbreviation contains the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army's hostels have an ancient doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonnade or covered portico of classical Greek building, which could serve as an entrance; ancient, hence old.

clue.text: Wash undergarment beside river

parts.note: a slip is a woman's undergarment
a stream is a small river

explanation.surface: Laundering your underwear down by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash' looks like a laundry verb but is a noun: the disturbed water behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipstream is the current of air or water left behind a moving craft, the same idea as a boat's wake.

clue.text: Charge one standing where fares are collected

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied
one is the Roman numeral I
rank means standing or status

explanation.surface: A fee for a single person standing at a ticket point.
explanation.definitionFit: Cab drivers queue at this spot to pick up their paying passengers, so it is where fares are found.

clue.text: Quack doctor used Post Office boxes

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the Post Office abbreviation goes round the rest
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of used are altered

explanation.surface: A fake physician used post office boxes for his business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' turns USED into SEUD, which the PO boxes. 'Quack' is an adjective here: fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Quack as an adjective means sham or fraudulent, the same sense as false or pretended.

clue.text: When extremely upset, some toss away the bones

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the two words read from the bottom up; the same letters inside toss away are no coincidence but the setter's second route, which some points at

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
so means extremely, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: When very annoyed, some people throw away the bones.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter gives two routes: 'some' also points to the letters within 'toss away', spelling the answer forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural for skeletal parts, seen in medical terms.

clue.text: An English record broadcast a lot, as the story goes

parts.note: taken as written
a CD is a record, a compact disc

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A British disc is played on air a lot, or so the tale goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns A LOT into OTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal describes something based on personal tales rather than evidence, just as a story tells it.

clue.text: Astronomical point perhaps isn't grasped

indicators.note: grasped means held within, so the answer lies inside the words perhaps isn't

explanation.surface: Maybe a point in astronomy has not been understood.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy this is either extreme of an orbit, its nearest or furthest point from the body it circles.

clue.text: Dream Queen Titian represented close to Padua

indicators.note: represented means shown in a new form, so the painter's name is rearranged
close to means the end of, so the last letter of Padua

explanation.surface: Titian painted a queen from a dream near Padua.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dream' is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; 'represented' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Early growth developed in Lima, Peru — not Spain

indicators.note: developed means grown into a new shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not means without, so the letter for Spain is dropped

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Something sprouted early in the Peruvian capital, but not in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes E from LIMA PERU, and 'developed' rearranges LIMAPRU.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula genus includes the primrose, whose name means first rose, among the earliest flowers of spring.

clue.text: Iris — first one replaced by yellow variety of it

indicators.note: first one replaced by means the opening I, the one, is swapped for the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: An iris whose first bloom is replaced by a yellow kind of iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the iris in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is a kind of iris whose root, orrisroot, is used in perfumery.

clue.text: Main dish of fish, as doctors ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of as doctors are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor's orders prescribe a big plate of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, not principal: these are tiny marine creatures that fish eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracods are minute crustaceans abundant in the ocean, food for fish, hence a dish of the main or sea.

clue.text: Dubious legal reason area's lacking cell units

indicators.note: dubious means doubtful or shaky, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means without, so the letter for area is dropped

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A doubtful legal argument lacks scope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes an A from LEGAL REASON, and 'Dubious' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Organelles are the specialised structures within a cell, such as mitochondria, each doing its own job.

clue.text: Doubt lovelorn patient eating porcino is married

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
lovelorn read as lacking love, love being zero, so the O goes

parts.note: a stoic is patient, enduring without complaint
the cep is the porcino mushroom
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lovesick patient eats a mushroom and gets married, to some doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovelorn' means without love, and love is zero (O) in tennis; 'eating' signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Scepticism is a questioning attitude, an unwillingness to believe without proof.

clue.text: I can't fathom this Athenian attitude to Cyprus

definitions.meaning: a confession that something is beyond understanding
taken literally, a Greek's claim on the island of Cyprus as wholly Greek territory

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by the Greek view of Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: Cyprus has a large Greek population and a long political dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom says something is completely incomprehensible, as if in a foreign tongue.

clue.text: Where cords strangely vibrate, not tense

indicators.note: vibrate means shake about, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so the letter for tense is dropped

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Somewhere vocal cords oddly quiver without strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' is the fodder, not an anagram signal; 'not tense' drops its T and 'vibrate' rearranges SRANGELY.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the voice boxes in the throat that house the vocal cords; the definition reaches into the wordplay.

clue.text: Private Russell's cheaper product

parts.note: own means private, as in one's own room
Russell Brand is a British comedian

explanation.surface: A soldier called Russell sells a budget product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an army rank. RUSSELL BRAND is a British comedian and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket goods sold under the shop's label, usually priced below the big names.

clue.text: Three worked on my back — it's bowed, for example

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters of three are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so my is turned round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Three people worked on my back, which is now bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' turns THREE into HETER; 'back' turns MY into YM.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spelt like another but said and meaning differently: bowed as in bent versus played with a violin bow.

clue.text: Artist in a lather?

parts.note: whimsically, a lather is one who works a lathe, and such a worker has the same name as the English painter J. M. W.

explanation.surface: A painter all worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a lather' suggests flustered; read as 'a lather' it is a lathe operator.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter J. M. W. shares his surname with a craftsman who shapes wood or metal on a lathe.

clue.text: Olivier et al keep working with English players

indicators.note: keep means hold within, so the abbreviation contains the other pieces

parts.note: the Olivier is one of the theatres of the National Theatre, NT, with others alongside
on means working, as in a machine being on

explanation.surface: Laurence Olivier and colleagues keep acting alongside English performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATIONAL THEATRE in London has three stages, one named the Olivier.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of nine musicians is a nonet, so players in an ensemble.

clue.text: Stirring hymns about debut of pretty young women

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled word goes round the other letter
stirring means mixing, so the letters of hymns are mixed
debut of means the first appearance, so the first letter of pretty

explanation.surface: Rousing hymns about the coming-out of pretty girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' turns HYMNS into NYMHS, and 'about' puts the P from 'debut of pretty' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nymphs are nature spirits of myth pictured as maidens, and by extension any attractive girls.

clue.text: A medic's way over somewhere near the kidneys

parts.note: taken as written
DR, doctor, is a medic

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for way is reversed

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A doctor's route crosses a spot close to the kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LANE into ENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys, the word itself meaning beside the kidney.

clue.text: Where primate holds beginning of service?

definitions.text: Where primate holds beginning of service?

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the animal goes round the letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of service

explanation.surface: Where an archbishop starts the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' is both the ape and an archbishop, who might begin worship from this end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, around the altar.

clue.text: Heroic, possibly involving origin of myths

definitions.text: Heroic, possibly involving origin of myths

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the shuffled letters go round another
possibly signals another arrangement of heroic's letters
origin means start, so the first letter of myths

explanation.surface: A brave deed that perhaps draws on legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns HEROIC into HOERIC, and 'involving' takes in the M from myths.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means epic and heroic in scale, like the poems of Homer full of myth.

clue.text: Someone who's admired lady's ring

parts.note: her is the possessive of a lady
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An admirer with a lady's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion or idol is looked up to by others for courage or achievement.

clue.text: Early column carried by wireless telegraphy

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the answer lies inside the words wireless telegraphy

explanation.surface: A newspaper column first sent by telegraph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' suggests journalism; it is a stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stele is an ancient upright stone slab or pillar, often inscribed.

clue.text: Doc's western pal? He's recruited about two auditors

parts.note: Wyatt Earp, Wild West lawman, was the friend of Doc Holliday

indicators.note: recruited means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written: HE plus S
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A Wild West question about a sidekick who has signed up a pair of listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Doc Holliday and Wyatt Earp fought together at the O.K. Corral.
explanation.definitionFit: Earphones come as a pair, one for each ear, and are what we listen with.
